newsitem.title: USA: Senate votes to increase Medicare eligibility age.
newsitem.headline: Senate votes to increase Medicare eligibility age.

text.p: The Senate voted Tuesday gradually to increase the Medicare eligibility age to 67 from the current 65, as lawmakers debated budget legislation making deep cuts in the popular health programme.
The Senate approved the politically charged change by a vote of 62-38. Under the plan, the higher eligibility age would not fully take effect until 2027.
Supporters argued the change would bring Medicare eligibility into line with Social Security and begin needed structural reforms to ensure Medicare's long-term solvency.

"This is a very, very modest approach to an extremely serious problem. What we were concerned about is the solvency of Medicare," said Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican. Senior citizens' groups opposed the move as a erosion of the government's commitment to Medicare, which provides health insurance to 38 million Americans.
The House did not include a similar provision in its version of the Medicare legislation and a tough battle is expected when congressional negotiators meet later this month to work out a final bill.
